answer: Use `clear [-f] topology [target=]<value>` in Operational mode; it manually removes existing topology neighbor information. The target is an instance-identifier (no default) and may be an lldp-neighbor instance discovered via LLDP, a carrier-neighbor instance discovered via ICMP, or an lldp-port-statistics instance holding the details of an LLDP-enabled port. Use 'clear topology <tab>' to list the valid topology objects, and the -f flag to force the command without confirmation. Example: clear topology lldp-neighbor-ethernet-1-4-T1-1. Reading is separate: `show topology` (also allowed in Candidate Configuration mode) takes inci, links, lldp, icdp or sndp.

Run `verify [-f] type-select=fiber-connection [target-select=<port-id>] [allow-switching]` in Operational mode. fiber-connection is currently the only verification type. target-select is the port instance-identifier on the CableID-capable sled; if it is omitted the verification runs on all paths, and if the port is in several CableID paths all of them are checked. allow-switching is boolean, default false: false verifies active paths only with no system-initiated switching (safe while in service); true allows CableID to initiate switching on the OPSM so both active and inactive paths are verified. Pre-condition: the equipment-policies cable-id-control attribute must be enabled. The command prompts for confirmation (-f skips it), is non-blocking, answers 'Verification started. Use show cable-id-status command to obtain latest verification status', and raises the CID-verification-in-progress alarm against the NE until all queued requests complete. Example: verify fiber-connection port-1-6-ade3 allow-switching=true

`bert` runs in Operational mode. Start with e.g. `bert start test-id=TestX resource=ethernet-1-6-T1 test-signal-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-monitoring-type=scrambled-idles test-signal-direction=ingress test-signal-monitoring-direction=ingress test-duration=10`, and stop with `bert stop test-id=TestX`; test-id is mandatory for the stop. test-id is alphanumeric [A-Z][a-z][0-9] and is system generated if you do not supply one. test-signal-type: none (default), PRBS31, PRBS31NONINV, scrambled-idles (100GE/400GE use scrambled-idles, ODU4 uses PRBS31/PRBS31NONINV). test-signal-monitoring-type adds fec-frames for CarrierCTP. Directions are ingress or egress. test-duration is in seconds, min 10 up to 1000 hrs, and 0 (the default) means indefinite. Multiple simultaneous BERTs can run on a facility. Records are read with `bert get` (by test-id, resource or AID) and removed with `bert delete`.

You cannot create one. The cid-ptp facility is created by the system when a card supporting the CableID function is created, for example RD20TM or CAD10A, and it represents the CableID SFP and its connection to the card via the CID port. managed-by reports 'system', and only user-created facilities can be user deleted, which is why the command set is just `set cid-ptp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]` and `show cid-ptp-<name>` (Operational and Candidate Configuration mode). admin-state is not editable and the only supported value is unlock; CableID operation is not affected by the cid-ptp admin-state. The 'used' attribute is true when CableID functionality is supported, false by default. Example: show cid-ptp-1-4-spcid, or show cid-ptp-1-6-spu for the CAD10A SPU port.

The eth-zr Digital Coherent 400ZR facility is auto-instantiated when the ZR TOM is provisioned; interface-type reads 400ZR (Media-interface 400ZR-CFEC-DP-16QAM) and rate 400.000 Gbit/s. fec-type is settable, default ofec, with permitted values not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4 (EFEC-I4), i7 (EFEC-I7), sdfec15 (15% SDFEC-Differential), sdfec15nd (15% SDFEC-Non-Differential), staircase7 (7% HDFEC Staircase) and ufec7 (7% UFEC). Degrade is controlled per alarm: fdd-monitoring and fed-monitoring (enabled/disabled, default disabled) enable FEC Detected Degrade and FEC Excessive Degrade monitoring. fdd-threshold defaults to 0.0195 avg BER and fdd-clear-threshold to 0.01062; fed-threshold defaults to 0.0206 avg BER and fed-clear-threshold to 0.01125. All four are decimal64(9) in the range 0.000000001..0.1 avg BER. link-degrade-indication shows none, local-degraded, remote-degraded or local-and-remote-degraded. Example: set eth-zr-1-6-T8 fed-threshold 0.011870000

The limit is the ethernet facility's max-packet-length attribute, the maximum transfer unit in octets, set with `set ethernet-<name> max-packet-length <value>`. The default is 1518 octets. The range is 1280..18000 octets on the 1830 GX G30 and 1518..18000 octets on the 1830 GX G40, so 18000 octets is the largest frame accepted. Two restrictions apply: max-packet-length is configurable at card level only and applies to all interfaces on that card, and it is used only for determining the undersized/oversized packet count in 100GbE PMs. The attribute is available with both set and show, in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

`show facilities` lists the facilities configured on the node. It takes no parameters and is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. The output is a flat list of facility instance names, for example on a 1830 GX G40: super-channel-group-1-4-L1, super-channel-1-4-L1-1, optical-carrier-1-4-L1-1, optical-channel-1-4-L1-1, trib-ptp-1-4-T11, comm-channel-1-4-L1-1, otu-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni, otu-1-4-T11, ethernet-1-4-T2, odu-1-4-L1-1-ODUCni, odu-1-4-L2-1-ODUflexi-1 and so on. Use the per-facility commands (show ethernet-<name>, show odu-<name>, etc.) for the attributes of any individual entry.

The Fibre Channel facility is managed with `set fc-<name>` / `show fc-<name>` in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. The FC-specific read-only attribute is fc-type, with values FC1G, FC2G, FC4G, FC8G, FC16G and FC32G. Two settable attributes are FC-specific to the 32GFC client: tts enables or disables Transmitter Training Signal support (enabled/disabled, default disabled), and laser-toggling-for-tts enables or disables laser toggling when tts is enabled/disabled for the 32GFC client (enabled/disabled, default enabled). The rest of the facility is the common client set: label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock), alarm-report-control, tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode (GMP default, plus BMP, openZR+, FlexE-4x100G, GFP-F, GFP-F-extOPU2, AMP, iGMP, none), loopback (none/facility/terminal), loopback-mode, and test-signal-type/direction (default ingress)/monitoring.

The flexo facility reports foic-type, the FOICx.k identification where k parallel lanes carry a FlexO-x interface and order x is the interface rate in units of 100G (G.709.3 FlexO-LR and G.709.1 FlexO-SR). The available types are foic1.2, foic1.4, foic2.4, foic2.8, foic3.6, foic4.8 and foic4.16, with foic4.8 as the default; foic-type is show only, as is fec-type (not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC; default ofec). resource-mode is settable and selects how the FlexO resource is used: ADM for add-drop, or XC for add-drop with regen. The default is ADM. Example: set flexo-1-5-L1-1 resource-mode 'XC'. Other settable attributes are label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, iid and the fdd/fed raise and clear thresholds.

`add flexo-group-<name> carriers <value> rate <value> modulation-format <value> group-id <value>` - name plus those four are the mandatory arguments; label, admin-state, alarm-report-control and fec-type are optional. carriers is the list of carriers bound to the facility, string length 1..32. rate is the carried signal basic rate class in Gbit/s. modulation-format is one of not-applicable, DP-QPSK, DP-16QAM, DP-8QAM, BPSK. group-id indicates the interface group instance the FlexO-x interface belongs to, an integer in the range 1..1048575, and it must be unique in the NE. fec-type defaults to ofec (values not-applicable, cfec, ofec, noFEC, G709, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7, ufec7); admin-state defaults to unlock. The command runs in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode, and `delete flexo-group-<name>` removes it.

`set high-speed-monitoring [enabled <value>] [port <value>]` and `show high-speed-monitoring [enabled] [port]`, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. It has exactly two attributes: enabled is the user configurable switch that turns high speed monitoring on or off, values true or false with a default of false; port is the user configurable port, a uint16 in the range 1..max with a default of 57500. So the command configures whether high speed monitoring runs and which port it uses, nothing else.

The interlaken facility represents the SPN2 Interlaken interface, managed with `set interlaken-<name>` / `show interlaken-<name>` in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Its capacity attribute is the total capacity of the Interlaken interface and is fixed and show only at 500 Gbit/s. The facility is system created (managed-by system), so you can only edit label (string 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited) and loopback (none by default, facility to test towards the facility side, terminal to test towards the terminal side). The remaining attributes - supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state, avail-state - are show only. Example: set interlaken-66-1-8 label interlaken_66_1

On line-ptp, auto-in-service is driven by two attributes usable on add, set and show. auto-in-service-enabled is the auto-in-service switch for the facility, true or false with a default of false. valid-signal-time is the configurable time that represents detection of a valid signal, used by the auto-in-service mechanism, a number in the range 1..7200 minutes with a default of 480. Once the mechanism is running, the show-only remaining-valid-signal-time reports the actual remaining time for the facility to be automatically enabled, in the same 1..7200 minute range. Example output: auto-in-service-enabled false, valid-signal-time 480 minutes, remaining-valid-signal-time 0 minutes. Both are also available on trib-ptp with the same ranges and defaults.

They are different commands. `show network-xconnect` is show only, has no parameters, and lists the services of multiple user cross connections commissioned in this NE; it runs in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. `nw-xconnect` is the configuration command for an individual networking cross-connection: `add nw-xconnect-<name> endpoint1 <value> endpoint2 <value> [xcon-type <value>] [rate <value>]`, plus `set nw-xconnect-<name> [rate <value>]`, `show nw-xconnect-<name>` and `delete nw-xconnect-<name>`. xcon-type is one of L1-ETH-TO-GCC0, L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 (default), L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC, and rate is 1..20 Mbps. So use network-xconnect to view the list and nw-xconnect to create, modify, view or delete a specific cross-connection.

nw-xconnect supports four user channel cross-connection types and there is no GCC-to-OSC combination among them: L1-ETH-TO-GCC0, L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 (the default), L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC. You can therefore bridge GCC0 to GCC0, OSC to OSC, or bring either onto an L1 Ethernet management port. Both endpoints are mandatory on creation. For L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 is an instance-identifier to a comm-eth MO of a chassis; for L1-GCC0-TO-GCC0 it is a GCC0 comm-channel MO and for L1-OSC-TO-OSC an OSCX-5 comm-channel MO. endpoint2 is a GCC0 comm-channel for the GCC0 types and an OSC-5 comm-channel for the OSC types. rate is 1..20 Mbps, defaulting to 13 for L1-ETH-TO-GCC0 and 20 for L1-ETH-TO-OSC and L1-OSC-TO-OSC. Example: add nw-xconnect-test1 xcon-type L1-ETH-TO-OSC endpoint1 comm-eth-1-16-ETH4 endpoint2 comm-channel-1-6-dwdm-line-OSCX5

No. The high order ODU is automatically created when an SCH is created; when a CHM6 has an OTU configured on it, use `show odu` to determine whether the ODU exists. What you create yourself are the low order ODUs, ODU4i (100G) or ODUflexi (400G), which the XCONs are mapped into. The pre-condition for that is that the super-channel must be added before low order ODUs can be added. Add them with `add odu-<name> odu-type <value>` plus parent-odu pointing at the parent HO-ODU name, and time-slots or opucn-time-slots (opucn-time-slots is optional and derived automatically if omitted). The show-only class attribute reports high-order, low-order (the default) or mapped, and is set by the system based on the order of creation. Example: add odu-1-1 odu-type ODU4i parent-odu '1-7-L1-1-ODUCni' time-slots 1..80

Yes. odu-diagnostics instances are keyed as `odu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction>` where direction is ingress or egress, and each direction has its own values, so you can set a different trace per direction with add, set, show and delete. Under tti-style ITU-T-G709 (the default) the TTI is split and you configure tx-sapi, tx-dapi and tx-operator with expected-sapi, expected-dapi and expected-operator; SAPI and DAPI are 1..15 printable ASCII characters (or a 0x hex string up to 32), operator bytes 1..32 (hex up to 66), all defaulting to "". Under tti-style proprietary the TTI is a single 64 byte string, configured through tx-tti and expected-tti (1..64 ASCII, or 0x hex up to 130). tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting selects the TIM criteria: disabled (default), full-64-bytes, SAPI, DAPI, OPER, SAPI-DAPI, SAPI-OPER, DAPI-OPER or SAPI-DAPI-OPER. Example: set odu-diagnostics-Lodu4i/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPIDAPI-OPER

Yes, FEC is on by default on an OTU. fec-mode, the configured Forward Error Correction mode on the OTUk/OTUCn client, takes enabled or disabled and defaults to enabled. fec-generation-mode, the FEC generation mode towards the far-end receiver, also takes enabled or disabled and defaults to enabled. fec-type defaults to ofec; the permitted values are not-applicable, cfec, ofec, G709, noFEC, i4, i7, sdfec15, sdfec15nd, staircase7 and ufec7. All three are available on add, set and show, in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode, for example `set otu-<name> fec-type ofec`. The related show-only service-mode-qualifier reports nofec when the transported payload carries no FEC.

Set tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting on the otu-diagnostics instance for the direction concerned: `set otu-diagnostics-<name>/<direction> tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI`, where direction is ingress or egress and each direction has its own values. The attribute says whether the TTI-Mismatch (TIM) alarm is reported or masked and, when reported, the criteria used. Values: disabled (the default), full-64-bytes, SAPI, DAPI, OPER, SAPI-DAPI, SAPI-OPER, DAPI-OPER and SAPI-DAPI-OPER. Choosing SAPI alarms only on a mismatched Source Access Point Identifier rather than the whole 64-byte trace. It requires tti-style ITU-T-G709 (the default), which splits the TTI into SAPI, DAPI and OPER bytes and uses expected-sapi/expected-dapi/expected-operator; these are mutually exclusive with the proprietary tx-tti/expected-tti buffer. Example: set otu-diagnostics-1-4-L1-1-OTUCni/ingress tti-mismatch-alarm-reporting SAPI

The stm facility carries the Synchronous Transport Module N signal (reference ITU-T G.691), and its show-only stm-type attribute lists exactly two SDH signal types: STM-16 and STM-64. The facility is managed with `set stm-<name>` / `show stm-<name>` in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Settable attributes include label, admin-state (Lock, Unlock, Maintenance; default Unlock), alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited), tx-mapping-mode and expected-mapping-mode, tti-style (ITU-T-G709 default, or proprietary), tim-monitor (enabled/disabled, default disabled), tx-tti and expected-tti (tti-64), loopback and loopback-mode (none, facility, terminal; default none), and test-signal-type (none by default; PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9, PRBS31) with test-signal-direction Ingress. Example: set stm-1-5-T9.2 tx-mapping-mode BMP

That is the trib-ptp tributary-disable-action attribute: it says what the network element does towards the client equipment connected over the TOM when a line-side failure is observed, either shutting off the laser or inserting a replacement signal. The values are laser-shut-off (the default), none, odu-ais, send-ais-1, send-gais, send-idles, send-lf, send-ms-ais, and send-nos for 1830 GX G30 only. tributary-disable-holdoff-timer delays that action at egress, uint16 0..10000 milliseconds with a default of 0 meaning holdoff disabled; it is applicable only when the TDA action is laser-turnoff, the recommendation being to hold the optical signal until the timer expires and only then turn off the laser. near-end-tda (default disabled) and tda-degrade-mode (BERSD-ODU triggering ALS, default disabled) refine it, and forward-defect-trigger (default true) decides whether a received client forward defect flows through to the line side or triggers an egress TDA action. Example: set trib-ptp-1-5-T2 tributary-disable-action laser-shut-off

Create it with `add xcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [payload-type <value>] [direction <value>] [label <value>] [circuit-id-suffix <value>]` in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode; source and destination are the instance IDs of the two end-points. direction supports only two-way, which is also the default. payload-type covers 100GBE, 400GBE, OTU4, 100G, ODU2, ODU2e and empty. Use `set xcon-<name>` for label and circuit-id-suffix, `show xcon-<name>` and `delete xcon-<name>`. protection-type is a show-only attribute reporting the protection this XCON has, with values y-cable, snc-n, snc-i and unprotected, the default being unprotected. Related show-only fields are type (add, drop, add-drop, express), payload-treatment (transport, switching, transport-without-fec, regen, regen-switching) and network-mapping. Example: add xcon-1 source ethernet-1-4-T1 destination odu-1-4-T1-1-ODUni-1

An L2-bridge is identified by bridge-name, a string of length 0..64 that forms the instance name in the command: `set L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name <value>] [description <value>]` and `show L2-bridge-<bridge-name> [chassis-name] [description]`, both available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. There are only two configurable attributes besides the name: chassis-name, a leafref giving the chassis associated with this L2 bridge, and description, a string of length 0..255 describing the bridge and its intended purpose. Neither has a default value.

Use `clear [-f] app [app-name=]<value>`. The clear app command clears third party apps, and app-name identifies the third party app to remove. The -f flag forces the command without confirmation. The command is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. app-name is the only parameter; the guide states no other values, ranges or defaults for it. To control rather than remove an application, use appctl with commands restart, netls or exec.

Use `appctl [app-name=]<value> [command=]<value> [[target=]<value>] [[parameters=]<value>[,<value>]*]` in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. app-name is a leafref to the configured third party app (path /ioa-ne:ne/ioa-ne:system/ioa-ne:sw-management/ioa-ne:third-party-app/ioa-ne:app-name). command is one of restart (restarts the third party application), netls (shows the list of subnet networks used by the containers) and exec (executes a third party application operation given in parameters); there is no default. target says whether the command is executed for the entire system or for a chassis/card AID, taking a string or 'system', and defaults to system. parameters holds optional values passed with the command, applicable when command is restart or exec, with a maximum of 50 elements.
